subject.title: [Bug]: sessions_yield subagent wake can compact parent branch at low context usage

question: Should OpenClaw add persisted compaction trigger metadata while also tightening successful-turn overflow decisions for parent sessions with suspect usage, or should the metadata be split into a separate follow-up?
rationale: The behavioral bug is source-supported, but the durable fix crosses provider usage semantics, compaction policy, and persisted transcript schema rather than a single mechanical patch.

options.title: Approve bounded runtime fix
options.body: Implement sane successful-turn overflow gating plus a closed compaction trigger field with focused regression tests and live subagent-yield proof.

options.title: Split trigger metadata
options.body: Fix false compaction first and leave persisted trigger attribution to a narrower schema/API design item.

options.title: Require live repro first
options.body: Hold implementation until a current-main canary reproduces the exact low-context sessions_yield compaction path after recent usage fixes.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded runtime fix
recommendation.body: Implement sane successful-turn overflow gating plus a closed compaction trigger field with focused regression tests and live subagent-yield proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent embedded OpenAI-compatible usage accounting work is closest to the surviving provider-independent usage path.
